description: A single-panel 3D isometric schematic (golden-yellow shaded solid model) of the flat, dog-bone test specimen used for both tensile and fatigue testing. The specimen is a long rectangular bar with a central reduced-width gauge section joined to two wider grip ends through curved shoulders. Dimension lines with arrowheads are drawn around the model: "55 mm" spans the overall specimen length; "15 mm" appears twice — one arrow across the left grip end and one across the central reduced section; "5 mm" marks the width of the reduced gauge section; "2.5 mm" marks the specimen thickness at the right end; and "R13 mm" labels the radius of the shoulder fillet between the gauge section and the right grip. A further dimension line at the lower-left is cropped by the image edge: only its "mm" unit is legible and its numerical value cannot be read. The drawing carries no material, phase or heat-treatment labels, no legend and no scale bar; it is purely a geometry definition. Read together with its caption, the panel fixes the specimen geometry shared by the wire-EDM-machined tensile and fatigue samples used in the study, whose loading/tensile axis is parallel to the rolling direction.

observations.observation: The figure is a 3D isometric schematic of a single flat dog-bone specimen, shown as a golden-yellow solid body with a central reduced-width gauge section between two wider grip ends bent at curved shoulders.
A dimension arrow labelled "55 mm" spans the overall length of the specimen.
Two separate "15 mm" dimension arrows are printed: one across the left grip end and one across the central reduced section.
"5 mm" is printed with an oblique arrow pointing to the width of the reduced gauge section.
"2.5 mm" is printed at the right end of the specimen, dimensioning its thickness.
"R13 mm" is printed at the lower right with a leader line to the shoulder, labelling the radius of the fillet between the reduced section and the grip.
A dimension line at the lower-left of the specimen is cropped by the image boundary; only its "mm" unit is legible and its numerical value cannot be read.
The schematic contains no material, phase, heat-treatment or sample-condition labels, no legend and no scale bar.
The caption states the figure is a schematic of sample shape and dimensions for tensile and fatigue tests.

The citing text states that flat dog-bone-shaped tensile samples were machined from sheets by wire electrical discharge machining (EDM) with their tensile axes parallel to the rolling direction, and that the tensile test samples are dimensioned in this figure.
The citing text states that the fatigue samples were also extracted by EDM with the loading axis parallel to the rolling direction and shared the same dimensions as the tensile samples.

The citing text states that tensile tests used a constant strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 and that stress-controlled tension-tension fatigue tests used a sinusoidal waveform at 20 Hz with a stress ratio R = 0.1; none of these test parameters are shown in the figure itself.

subfigures.description: 3D isometric drawing of one flat dog-bone specimen (golden solid body) with printed dimension callouts: 55 mm overall length, two 15 mm lengths (left grip end and central reduced section), 5 mm gauge-section width, 2.5 mm thickness at the right end, and R13 mm shoulder fillet radius. A slightly inclined central reduced (gauge) section connects two wider, flat grip ends. No material labels or scale bar. One lower-left dimension line is cropped and unreadable.
